chapter_title: Chương 231: 0232【Kèm theo một phiên dịch đồng thời cũng được】

segments.title: Chương 231: 0232【Kèm theo một phiên dịch đồng thời cũng được】
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang didn't go to the ticket lottery, mainly because his English was terrible and he couldn't understand what An Nan was saying.

Chen Guiliang hadn't even passed the College English Test Band 4 yet.

In the afternoon, he skipped class again and made a trip to the company.

"How have things been the last two days?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chi Siyuan said, "The whitelist and blacklist system is still being perfected. You could also say we're mutually adapting. Those who like to comment on current events and curse people out will automatically adapt to the standards of each website. Only the rumor-mongers are hard to deal with, because it's difficult to determine if they're actually spreading rumors."

"That one who was spreading rumors for several days straight, how did you find him?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chi Siyuan said, "At the end of every article, he'd add the note 'For internal exchange, to be used for rumor-mongering.' He was trying to absolve himself while encouraging others to cite his articles to spread rumors."

"Is this guy a f*cking psycho?" Chen Guiliang couldn't help but retort.

Chi Siyuan said, "I also copied his articles and Baidu-searched a few keywords. I found quite a few forums and Tieba posts that cited his articles to spread rumors. After he ignored multiple warnings, I've already banned his account. Now that guy has gone to other blogs and is spreading rumors and cursing us out every day."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What about that Fang Zhouzi?"

Chi Siyuan said, "This person is very clever. After being warned twice, he more or less figured out our standards. He can't be bothered to write new articles, so he's just been copying and pasting the old column pieces he published in newspapers."

Chi Siyuan added, "On Hainei Net's trending list these past two days, the top two spots are all related to the Qier Pharmaceutical fake drug incident. It's even pushed the completion of the Three Gorges Dam, the UEFA Champions League Final, and *Super Girl* further down. Many people are fanning the flames using the fake drug incident, leaving our content moderators completely bewildered, unable to tell which news is real and which is fake."

This couldn't be helped. If they couldn't tell, they could only leave it alone for now. Casually deleting posts or banning users would only stir up a bigger public outcry.

Chen Guiliang returned to his own office, and Ao Yanchang followed him in with a folder. "After consulting with Professor Wu and Professor Zhang, this is the company restructuring plan I've drawn up based on your requirements and the company's actual situation."

Now that they had secured a huge amount of venture capital and the website was growing ever larger, the previous makeshift structure had to be adjusted accordingly.

ByteDance's next step was to expand its workforce to about 150 people.

The company's departments would be refined along four lines: Product & Technology, Operations & Growth, Commercialization, and Functional Support.

Of course, some departments would not be established immediately.

For example, the legal department wasn't officially established. It was just expanded from the previous single legal specialist to a three-person legal team.

Chen Guiliang carefully reviewed the plan. After discussing the details with Ao Yanchang, he made two changes and then briskly signed it.

Next, Chen Guiliang sent someone to Shancheng to discuss investing in Zhubajie.com with Zhu Mingyao.

He then called in several senior executives and heads of important functions one by one, chatting with them individually about their recent work and the upcoming company restructuring.

After handling matters at ByteDance, Chen Guiliang went downstairs to Game Science.

Game Science's chief steward, Qu Guohao, though not as rich in theoretical knowledge as Ao Yanchang, was much more adept when it came to practical execution.

Qu Guohao could basically complete any task Chen Guiliang assigned with guaranteed quality and quantity, and there was usually little else that Chen Guiliang needed to worry about.

Game Science was also hiring more staff recently, with a plan to reach a scale of 100 people.

Besides *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, which was constantly making money, there was also YKpay. Xiaonei Net, Hainei Net, and Quan Yu Tian Xia were all partnered with YKpay, earning a cut from top-ups every day.

Because online banking payments were such a pain, the percentage of users on *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, Xiaonei Net, and Hainei Net who used YKpay was getting higher and higher.

However, YKpay also had frequent problems. Dong Qianqiu was patching it up every few days and was currently leading a technical team to develop YKpay 2.0.

Among the new hires in Game Science's expansion were three programmers specifically recruited for the YKpay 2.0 team.

The casual card and board games on the Game Science Interactive Games Platform had also started to turn a profit. But the profits weren't even a fraction of what *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* made; they were mainly using them to build up a user base.

Flash games and browser games were much like the card and board games. They had a large player base, but very few were willing to pay.

The number of domestic standalone games for sale on the Game Science Interactive Games Platform had increased to 17. The cumulative total sales were still less than 500 copies, and it was unlikely the situation would turn around in the short term, because pirated versions of all these games were available for download!

If you could download a pirated copy, who would use the official version?

Chen Guiliang once again called in the department heads for talks. The last one to be called in was Meng Zicong, the project lead for *Future Era*.

Meng Zicong reported, "The engine and game production have entered the third phase. We estimate that in another two to three months, we'll be able to move into full-scale production and engine optimization."

Chen Guiliang didn't understand any of that and asked directly, "When can it reach the closed beta stage?"

"Eight to twelve months," Meng Zicong said.

Chen Guiliang mentally calculated the timeline and found the development speed was far beyond his expectations. He had thought it would take at least 15 months.

Meng Zicong, however, thought Chen Guiliang felt it was too slow and quickly said, "Boss, everyone is already working very hard. If we need to rush, we can work more overtime."

At this time, the development cycle for domestically self-developed games was basically under a year.

Games like *Quan Yu Tian Xia* and *Zhengtu*, which took over a year, were considered outliers.

Meanwhile, *Future Era*, from preparation to completion, was estimated to take 20 months. This far exceeded the development cycle of domestic online games!

"It's fine, just focus on perfecting it. There's no need to intentionally work overtime for now," Chen Guiliang said.

Not working overtime was impossible.

The *Future Era* project team had been working overtime for a while now, and it was genuinely the employees staying behind voluntarily. For instance, if someone hadn't finished their work for the day, or if they needed to adjust some details, it was common for them to stay and work overtime for two or three hours.

This, in turn, created a difficult situation for Chen Guiliang to handle.

Paying more overtime wages was equivalent to encouraging overtime.

This would send the wrong signal that the boss wanted employees to work more overtime.

As the company grew larger, some mid-level or senior managers might start demanding even more overtime from employees just to please their superiors. They might even stay late to "perform" even after finishing their day's work.

Efficiency wouldn't improve much, but the employees would be full of complaints.

But overtime pay still had to be given; after all, he couldn't have employees working for free.

In the end, Chen Guiliang set a few rules:

First, for overtime required in special, urgent situations, a signature from a corresponding senior executive was required. Overtime pay would be three times the normal wage.

Second, for overtime without an executive's signature, there was a weekly overtime limit for each specific employee. If the limit was exceeded, employees could report it anonymously, and the department or team lead would be held accountable. This type of overtime pay was only 1.5 times the normal wage.

Third, during overtime, the company would provide meals and a transportation allowance.

For a transmigrator like Chen Guiliang, making money was too easy. And there was no end to the money one could make, so there was no need to adopt a 996 model.

When he was just starting out, Chen Guiliang had to be frugal, and was even teased by Ao Yanchang for being a capitalist.

Now, he had bounced back.

With Chen Guiliang's new policy, aside from a few who still liked to slack off, the overall morale of the employees was on the rise.

It was true that comparison is the thief of joy. Compared to other internet companies, ByteDance and Game Science were practically heaven.

Now, anyone who was asked to stay for overtime would do so with a laugh, without any emotional distress.

Meng Zicong couldn't help but ask, "Boss, have you ever come across *DNF* before?"

"Huh?" Chen Guiliang feigned ignorance.

Meng Zicong said, "There's a game in South Korea called *DNF*, and its gameplay is very similar to our *Future Era*. Of course, only the gameplay is similar; the content is completely different."

"*DNF* is very popular in Korea?" Chen Guiliang asked, feigning ignorance again.

Meng Zicong said, "Some Chinese students studying in Korea have been posting *DNF* screenshots on gaming forums, and they've even created a DNF Tieba. I secretly downloaded the game and played on the Korean server for a few days, and I got a lot of inspiration from *DNF*."

Chen Guiliang said, "I've heard of *DNF* as well. But when I was planning *Future Era*, *DNF* hadn't even launched in Korea yet. It's a pure coincidence."

"I know it's a coincidence," Meng Zicong said with concern, "but what if a domestic game company brings *DNF* to China? By then, our *Future Era* won't be finished yet, and we'll have our thunder stolen by *DNF*! So, I'm requesting to lift the weekly overtime limit so we can get *Future Era* done as soon as possible!"

Chen Guiliang shook his head and said, "There's no need. *DNF* won't be coming to China anytime soon."

"Why?" Meng Zicong asked.
